segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the start of all things, before any person drew breath, a counsel happened in the Godhead — let us make man in our image.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Hear the word us. God is not talking to himself there — he is talking with someone, and what they decide together is to make a creature that looks like them. Then he hands that creature the whole living world to take care of.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And then he did it. Not one of them closer to God than the other. Both of them bearing the likeness.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The plan included dominion — over fish, birds, cattle, and all the earth. Stewards, not owners.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Not in the shape of any creature, but bearing something of God himself:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the capacity to know him, to choose him, to reflect him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Every person since carries that original dignity — made in the image, loved into being.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You are made in his image. That is worth more than you know.
